Q: X32dbg Parsing Command Line Failures A:

Use x64dbg's breakpoint log text, not dd ... L1. dd is an assembly pseudo-instruction, not a format string!

For kernel32.WriteFile:

bp kernel32.WriteFile
bplog kernel32.WriteFile, "ret={p:[esp]} len={x:[esp+C]}"
bpcond kernel32.WriteFile, 0

For KERNELBASE.WriteFile:

bp KERNELBASE.WriteFile
bplog KERNELBASE.WriteFile, "ret={p:[esp]} len={x:[esp+C]}"
bpcond KERNELBASE.WriteFile, 0

Why:

bp only sets the breakpoint. bplog sets the log format string for an existing software breakpoint, and x64dbg command arguments are comma-separated, not space-separated. The formatter syntax is {type:expression}; [esp] dereferences the return address, and [esp+C] dereferences nNumberOfBytesToWrite. (See also formatting docs!)

Setting bpcond ..., 0 makes it log without stopping. You can omit the bpcond command if you want to actually break at that point and log it.

In general, I recommend studying the docs, all the commands are explained there!

Q: Content type 'application/octet-stream' not supported A:

I was facing the same issue with the Swagger API because of the Content-Type. I copied the cURL request from Swagger and pasted it into Postman, and it worked successfully. So, it seems the issue is with the Swagger documentation/configuration. Your API should work correctly during frontend integration.

Q: Using github actions to create a .zip file in main branch A:

Add the following step:

  - name: Commit and push
    uses: EndBug/add-and-commit@v7
    with:
      add: '["folder.zip"]'
      message: 'My commit message'
      push: true

Q: Runtime error '3705': opertion is not allowed when the object is open A:

Another potential cause is that rs already has a recordset open. Because your code doesn't Dim and initialize rs inside of your method I'm assuming it's created as a module variable and it doesn't look like it's being closed.

Somewhere you need to call rs.Close before you can call rs.Open again. Add this before your rs.Open line and run your code.

If Not rs.State = adStateClosed Then
    MsgBox "The recordset is already open"
End If

Q: Could the L1 Cache Save Computation Time? A:

Func mul(a b) over small LookUp Tables with precalculated results

BENCHMARK TEST CONDITIONS

* Iterations:              50,000,000 runs per test method
* Input Data:              Pre-generated random numbers within the 0 to 127 range (inclusive)
* Multiplier:              Fixed (value: 7)
* LookUp Table Size Type1: 128 elements (512 bytes total per table for int/uint types)
* LookUp Table Size Type2: 128 elements (128 bytes total per table for sbyte/byte types)
* Memory Allocation:       Unmanaged OS heap via Marshal.AllocHGlobal (bypassing .NET GC)
* Alignment:               64-byte boundaries (strictly matched to CPU cache line size)
* Access Method1:          Direct unsafe pointers (int*/uint*) without bounds checking
* Access Method2:          Direct unsafe pointers (sbyte*/byte*) without bounds checking
* Target Runtime:          .NET 8/9 (Release Build, x64 architecture)

PERFORMANCE TEST RESULTS (50M ITERATIONS)

Data Type | Method                  | ~Time    | ~Speed      | CPU-Level Mechanics

int       | Multiply Function (CPU) | 14-17 ms | 100% (Base) | Executes hardware imul
int       | Unmanaged LUT (Aligned) | 13-16 ms | ~105% Fast  | Direct L1 read

uint      | Multiply Function (CPU) | 14-17 ms | 100% (Base) | Executes hardware mul
uint      | Unmanaged LUT (Aligned) | 13-16 ms | ~105% Fast  | Direct L1 read

PERFORMANCE TEST RESULTS (50M ITERATIONS)

Data Type | Method                  | ~Time    | ~Speed      | CPU-Level Mechanics

sbyte     | Multiply Function (CPU) | 20-24 ms | 100% (Base) | Requires sign extension (movsx)
sbyte     | Unmanaged LUT (Aligned) | 13-16 ms | ~150% Fast  | Instant L1 read via 2 cache lines

byte      | Multiply Function (CPU) | 18-22 ms | 100% (Base) | Requires zero extension (movzx)
byte      | Unmanaged LUT (Aligned) | 15-19 ms | ~150% Fast  | Instant L1 read via 2 cache lines

Incredible results yea?

Q: How do I generate random words from two different lists and combine them into one search? A:
  1. You generate a random number between 0 and [size of list]. We call this randomIndex. You then select the item from list X at randomIndex and return it.
  2. Now armed with the algorithm 'pick a random item from a list', we apply it to list A. then we apply it to list B. Voila. a random word from two different lists.
  3. String.format(""""%s" AND "%s" site:.edu""", pickRandom(listA), pickRandom(listB)).

This is beyond trivial stuff. I'm assuming, because you're asking, there are complications, but these are not mentioned in your question. This is simple enough that the concept of 'best practice' doesn't really apply to the situation. Any more than it would for the question "how do I add 2 single-digit numbers together". You just.. do.

Q: Handle Cloudflare Turnstile on Inglatan Website A:

Instead of forcing GUI click, let SeleniumBase handle the reconnection, and bypas completely natively by navigating and giving the Ubderdetected Chromedriver (UC) space to handle the cookies/tokens without explicit actions.

import time
from seleniumbase import Driver

driver = Driver(uc=True, headless=False) 

url = "https://ingatlan.com/35386626"

driver.uc_open_with_reconnect(url, reconnect_time=6)

time.sleep(10)


try:
    driver.verify_success()  # Waits until the anti-bot page disappears
except Exception:
    # Fallback: let it click only if verify_success didnt auto-pass
    driver.uc_gui_click_captcha()

time.sleep(10)
print("Page title:", driver.title)
driver.quit()
